You’re busy crafting quality content and mastering your social media strategy. You don’t have _time_ to exhaustively compile a list of the ideal length of social media posts for every single platform.

So we did it for you. (Please, hold your applause.)

This isn’t just a list of how long social posts _can_ be: it’s a list of the best social media post lengths to drive the most engagement.

If you want more likes, shares, video views, and comments (and what kind of monster doesn’t?!), it’s pivotal to nail the length of your message.

Are you writing too much in your social media posts? Too little? Are your [videos too long or not long enough](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-video-length/)? Read on for our curated research on the ideal character counts for social media posts (not to be confused with character limits) and other types of content on:

- Facebook
- X (formerly Twitter)
- Instagram
- TikTok
- LinkedIn
- Youtube
- Pinterest
- Snapchat

TL;DR: Optimize the length of your content, and you’ll be more likely to engage and convert your audience. Let’s go.

# **The ideal length of social media posts**

## **The ideal Facebook post length**

While you have enough space to craft a short novella on FB, the truth is, shorter posts usually receive more likes, comments, and shares.

People like it when a message makes its point quickly and concisely. It’s satisfying.

### **Organic posts length: 1 to 80 characters**

We scoured the World Wide Web for research, and the most recent study is from way back in 2016… an eternity in Social Media Years. But it’s all we have to work with, so it makes the best starting point we have:

In 2016, BuzzSumo analyzed more than 800 million Facebook posts. Based on [their findings](http://buzzsumo.com/blog/ultimate-guide-facebook-engagement-2017/), posts with less than 50 characters “were more engaging than long posts.” According to another, more precise [study by Jeff Bullas](https://www.jeffbullas.com/10-powerful-tips-to-increase-fan-engagement-on-facebook/), **posts with 80 characters or fewer receive 66% higher engagement**.

There are a couple of reasons for this…

**Barrier to entry:** Facebook cuts off longer posts with an ellipsis, forcing users to click “See More” to expand the text and read the entire message.

This extra step may not seem like much, but it will reduce engagement. Every time you ask the audience to take action, a percentage of people will lose interest.

**Barrier to comprehension:** The longer a person reads, the harder his or her brain must work to process information. Content that demands less work to consume and understand will enjoy higher engagement rates.

### **Paid posts length: 5 to 19 words**

Every Facebook ad needs three types of content: a Headline, Ad Text, and a Link Description.

After [analyzing 752,626 Facebook ads](https://adespresso.com/blog/we-analyzed-37259-facebook-ads-and-heres-what-we-learned/) back in 2018, AdEspresso found that ads did best when the copy in each element was clear and concise. According to the data, the ideal length for a:

- **Headline**, the first text people read, is 5 words.
- **Ad text**, which appears above the ad, is 19 words
- **Link description**, which appears below the headline, is 13 words

The bottom line: Whether the post is organic or paid, brevity seems to drive engagement.

Capitalize on this by keeping your ad copy concise: don’t use two words when one will do. And keep it clear: omit adverbs, jargon, and the passive voice from your copy.

### **Video length: 30 to 60 seconds**

Sure, you _can_ upload a 240-minute video to Facebook… but will anyone actually watch it all the way through? With video, one of the primary measures of success is how long people watch, also known as your [video retention rate](https://www.facebook.com/formedia/blog/understanding-how-your-videos-perform-on-facebook).

For viral content, Facebook recommends videos that are less than one minute or stories that are less than 20 seconds in length.

That said, if you’re hoping to qualify for in-stream ads, you might want to linger a little longer — videos need to be over three minutes to qualify.

Facebook also recommends videos over three minutes for episodic series, live streaming, or story development.

Careful! Don’t go over the limit:

| Facebook Text | Character Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Facebook Post | 63,206 |
| Username | 50 |
| Page Description | 255 |
| Facebook Ad Headline | 40 |
| Facebook Ad Text | 135 |
| Facebook Link Description | 30 |

## **The ideal length of a post on X**

So, how many characters are in an X post (formerly known as a tweet)? Back in 2017, Twitter doubled its character limit from 140 to 280 to help make writing on the platform easier.

Still, just because you have twice the room doesn’t mean people want to see you use it.

### **Organic and promoted post length: 71 – 100 characters**

Whether you’re running an ad or not, data from [Buddy Media](https://techcrunch.com/2012/06/09/7-things-buddy-media-did-right-to-become-an-800mm-company/) shows that X posts containing less than 100 characters receive, on average, 17 percent higher engagement than longer tweets.

This is, in part, because shorter posts are easier to read and comprehend.

There is a way to get around the character limit on X:

Back in 2022, Warby Parker cleverly combined a long list of short tweets to get the best of both worlds by creating a long thread for the longest day of the year: quick and cheeky content, delivered in a large volume.

### **X hashtag length: 6 characters**

“The best hashtags are those composed of a single word or a few letters,” writes Vanessa Doctor from Hashtags.org. “Experts recommend keeping the keyword under 6 characters.”

Again, this length is about reader comprehension, especially since hashtags don’t support spaces.

## **The ideal TikTok video length**

People have downloaded TikTok [more than 3 billion times](https://blog.hootsuite.com/tiktok-stats/), which means you’ve got a lot of short attention spans out there in the world to appease.

For most users, the max video length on TikTok is [10 minutes,](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-updates/tiktok/tiktok-long-form-content/) though the platform has been experimenting with video lengths of 20, 30, and even 60 minutes.

But just because you _can_ do something doesn’t necessarily mean you should. On TikTok, brevity thrives.

### **Organic TikTok video length: 7 to 15 seconds**

To hook a viewer and keep their attention, **aim for a 15-second video**.

The more people who watch and like your video, the more likely you are to appear on someone else’s [For You Page](https://blog.hootsuite.com/tiktok-for-you-page/), so it’s important to really knock it out of the park. (For more on [appeasing the great TikTok algorithm, click here.](https://blog.hootsuite.com/tiktok-algorithm/))

That said, you may still want to try out TikTok’s [7-second challenge](https://blog.hootsuite.com/experiment-7-second-tiktok-challenge/). When our social team tried it, their video received half a million views —not too shabby at all.

### **TikTok ads length: 21 to 24 seconds**

For top performance of ads, TikTok [recommends](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/creativecenter/insight/creativeinsight/pc/en?rid=2ak7hkp8i9&lang=en) 21-34 seconds.

But of course, length isn’t everything: content and quality formatting matter, too. We’ve got the rundown of [everything you need to become a TikTok ads master right here.](https://blog.hootsuite.com/tiktok-advertising/)

## **Ideal LinkedIn post length**

More than [1 billion professionals](https://blog.hootsuite.com/linkedin-statistics/) use LinkedIn, and as the platform’s user base grows, it becomes increasingly difficult to win organic attention. Marketers must continually optimize their messaging for quality, [timing](https://blog.hootsuite.com/best-time-to-post-on-social-media/), and of course, length.

### **Organic and paid updates length: 25 words**

The research on this topic isn’t very recent, but Hootsuite finds that, as with all other types of social updates, it’s best to keep LinkedIn updates short.

The LinkedIn post character limit before the “See More” button is 140. Your message will be cut off at the 140-character mark — like Shopify’s ad here did.

![shopify plus ultimate guide to site speed](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-length-01.png)

As a general rule of thumb, we stick to 25 words or fewer. In fact, we’d recommend making sure your message is clear within the first 150 characters.

### **Article length: 1,900 to 2,000 words**

Paul Shapiro, founder of Search Wilderness, analyzed more than 3000 of the most successful posts on LinkedIn’s publishing platform. These posts, on average, received 42,505 views, 567 comments, and 138,841 likes.

He discovered that articles with more words perform better.

“Posts between 1900 and 2000 words perform the best,” [writes](https://noahkagan.com/linkedin-publishing-success/) Shapiro. “\[They\] gain the greatest number of post views, LinkedIn likes, LinkedIn comments, and LinkedIn shares.”

Shapiro also learned that the ideal LinkedIn character limit for titles is between 40 and 49 characters. Titles in this range received the greatest number of post views overall.

### **Video length: 30 seconds**

In 2017, LinkedIn gave its users the ability to natively upload videos that play automatically in their followers’ feeds. Unlike other platforms, LinkedIn also shares video data (e.g., viewers’ companies and job titles), making it a valuable resource for marketers.

[According to LinkedIn](https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions/success/best-practices/video-ad-tips), the most successful video ads are less than 15 seconds long. However, the lengths can vary when it comes to a native LinkedIn video.

For brand awareness and brand consideration videos, LinkedIn recommends keeping the length under 30 seconds.

Meanwhile, videos that meet upper-funnel marketing goals should stick to a 30 to 90-second video length.

## **The ideal Instagram post length**

Unlike Facebook and X, Instagram was founded on visual content. The platform was made to showcase compelling pictures and videos, but the right combination of words will promote engagement on any post.

Engagement, of course, is crucial to maximizing your content’s reach, since [Instagram’s algorithm](https://blog.hootsuite.com/instagram-algorithm/) places posts with the most likes and comments near the top of your followers’ feeds.

### **Organic Instagram post caption length: 138 to 150 characters**

A successful Instagram caption adds context, shows off your brand’s personality, entertains audiences, and compels your followers to take action.

[![Instagram caption Vancouver houses side-by-side](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-post-length-02-620x229.jpg)](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-post-length-02.jpg)

The Instagram caption limit is 2,200 characters. But you’ll only need a fraction of that limit to move the needle (as our [very scientific experiment about caption lengths can attest](https://blog.hootsuite.com/long-instagram-captions-experiment/)).

Most people scroll through their feed quickly, so it makes sense to keep your captions clear, concise, and punchy.

Brief copy is easy to consume. It also doesn’t get cut off with an ellipsis. Need some writing inspo? [Find 311 creative Instagram captions to get you started right here.](https://blog.hootsuite.com/instagram-captions-drive-engagement/)

### **Sponsored Instagram post caption length: 125 characters or less**

Instagram recommends keeping the captions on sponsored posts under 125 characters.

Again, this length supports readability and ensures that the text won’t get truncated.

Looking for more inspiration? Here are [53 examples of amazing Instagram ads](https://adespresso.com/blog/37-instagram-ads-examples/).

### **Instagram video length: 15 seconds**

Most people will watch your Instagram video (organic or advertisement) on their phones, so following best practices for mobile video length is important if you wanna keep the viewer’s attention.

That means keeping videos here to 15 seconds or less. Short! And! Sweet!

[Find more best practices for Instagram ads here.](https://blog.hootsuite.com/instagram-ads-guide/#Best_practices_for_Instagram_ads)

### **Instagram hashtags: 3-5 per post, at fewer than 24 characters each**

Instagram posts can have up to 30 hashtags, making it tempting to stuff each caption with as many as possible. As a marketer, fight this urge. Using more hashtags won’t necessarily yield higher visibility.

In fact, Instagram revealed that 3-5 hashtags will actually get you the best results, and [our own little experiment confirmed just that](https://blog.hootsuite.com/experiment-instagram-hashtags/).

[![Instagram Creator hashtag best practices](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-post-length-03-620x453.png)](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-post-length-03.png)

_Source:_ [_@creators_](https://www.instagram.com/p/CUV20kxvLgS/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link)

Of course, picking the _right_ hashtags to use is a whole other story. Our [guide to Instagram hashtags](https://blog.hootsuite.com/instagram-hashtags/) will walk you through your options.

### **Instagram Stories length: 7 to 15 seconds**

Instagram’s parent company, Meta, notes that people consume Stories much faster than other content, so it’s important to capture their attention right off the bat.

You’ve really only got 15 seconds to work with — that’s the maximum length of an Instagram Story — so hit the ground running.

### **Instagram Reels length: 7 to 15 seconds**

While [Reels](https://blog.hootsuite.com/experiment-what-reels-caption-length-gets-the-best-engagement/) can be much longer than Stories — up to a minute in length for most people, and 90 seconds for select beta-testers —that same short-attention-span principle applies here. Get to the point quickly and keep it short.

Careful! Don’t go over the limit:

| Instagram Text | Instagram Character Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Caption (Organic) | 2,200 |
| Caption (Sponsored) | 255 |
| Hashtag Limit | 30 hashtags |
| Reels Caption | 2,200 |
| Ad Text | 2,200 |
| Bio | 150 |
| Username | 30 |

## **The ideal length for YouTube posts**

At the end of the day, YouTube is a search engine, meaning it relies on text to organize and rank the [nearly 500 hours of video](https://www.statista.com/statistics/259477/hours-of-video-uploaded-to-youtube-every-minute/) uploaded to its servers every minute.

Therefore, in addition to optimizing video length, marketers must front load their content’s title and description copy with relevant keywords—and that means keeping an eye on character count.

### **YouTube video length: 7 to 15 minutes**

Whether you’re watching videos on YouTube or anywhere else, one of the most important KPIs is retention.

How long do people actually watch? Are viewers finishing your videos at a high rate? If so, you’re doing something right.

Statista reports that the average video is [11.7 minutes long](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1026923/youtube-video-category-average-length/), and the Social Media Examiner endorses this as the ideal, writing that videos between [7 and 15 minutes](https://www.socialmediaexaminer.com/15-tips-growing-youtube-channel/) have the best performance.

Here’s one that’s nine minutes, for instance. Ooh! Ahh!

Of course, there’s more to a successful YouTube strategy than just the right length for your video. Here’s everything you need to know about [creating great YouTube content for your business.](https://blog.hootsuite.com/youtube-marketing/)

### **YouTube title length: 70 characters**

The **most important SEO factor to consider for YouTube is the title of your video**.

Include relevant keywords to make sure you’re reaching high rankings in Google and YouTube search, while simultaneously being compelling enough to encourage clicks and views.

![J.J. McCullough relevant keywords YouTube titles](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-post-length-04.png)

It’s a tall order! And, P.S., it should be pretty tightly crafted: Influencer Marketing Hub suggests keeping it to 70 characters maximum so that it doesn’t get cut off.

If you need help honing your YouTube title, we’ve got a free AI tool that’ll do it for you. Check out our [YouTube title generator](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/ai-youtube-title-generator-free) for the quickest path to video success.

### **YouTube description length: 150 characters**

The first 100 to 150 characters will appear under your video, so optimize that chunk of text with both rich description and lots of intriguing keywords.

Hone your description-writing skills with our [YouTube caption guide](https://blog.hootsuite.com/youtube-descriptions/) or head straight to our handy [AI-powered YouTube video description generator](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/youtube-video-description-generator).

Careful! Don’t go over the limit:

| YouTube Text | Characters |
| --- | --- |
| Video Title | 100 |
| Video Description | 5,000 |
| Username | 20 |
| Bio | 1,000 |
| Playlist Title | 100 |

## **The ideal size and length for Pinterest posts**

On Pinterest, image size matters. So does the length of your description.

### **Pinterest images: 1000 X 1500 pixels**

According to [Pinterest best practices](https://business.pinterest.com/en-ca/creative-best-practices/), images on the platform should have a 2:3 aspect ratio, which is how the height and width of an image relate.

### **Description length: 200 characters**

[Studies](https://socialmarketingwriting.com/how-to-write-a-pinterest-pin-description/) show that descriptions containing about 200 characters receive the most repins. (For more juicy numbers, [check out our guide to must-know Pinterest stats here](https://blog.hootsuite.com/pinterest-statistics/).)

Your Pinterest caption is your chance to add context, persuade, and sell. It’s your chance to tell a story and conjure emotion, to make a promise. The description is your chance to compel.

## **The ideal length of Snapchat videos and captions**

Given how brief the limits are on Snapchat captions and videos, it’s almost impossible to go _too_ long.

To really thrive with engagement on this platform, it’s really more about _what_ you’re posting, not how long that content plays for.

### **Ideal Snapchat Story length: 15 seconds**

Snapchat Story videos can be up to 60 seconds long, but it’s pretty rare for engagement to be high for those (relatively) long-form pieces of content.

Instead, aim for (we’ve said it before, and we’ll say it again!) short-and-sweet videos that hit hard off the top, like this hot sauce ad, which clocks in at just 20 seconds but [makes a serious impact](https://forbusiness.snapchat.com/inspiration/hot-sauce-brand-truff-achieves-massive-roi-on-snapchat?utm_source=GoogleSEM&utm_medium=PAIDB2B&utm_campaign=Brand&utm_term=CA&utm_content=SuccessStories).

![hot sauce 20 second Snapchat ad](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/ideal-social-media-post-length-05.png)

New to Snapchat? Here’s our guide to [Snapchat for Business for beginners](https://blog.hootsuite.com/how-to-use-snapchat-beginners-guide/).

### **Ideal Snapchat video caption length: 50 characters**

Captions for snaps can be up to 80 characters, but they’re really secondary to the visual content, so don’t stress too much about making the most of this.

## Ad features

- **Use add overlay to create image template:** Image template is an Advantage+ creative enhancement that allows you to customize the color and font of your text and present it in a banner template on your ad. This helps your text stand out in your own brand color and preferred font in your ad. [Learn more about Advantage+ creative enhancements](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/297506218282224).

- **Use add text overlay:** Text overlay is a generative AI enhancement in Advantage+ creative that allows you to apply different text overlays onto your uploaded ad creative. [Learn more about Advantage+ creative enhancements](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/297506218282224).

- **Use text generation:** Text generation is a generative AI feature that allows you to generate up to 5 variations of your primary text and headline based on your original primary text and headline inputs for your ad. [Learn more about text generation](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/497610041230617).

- **Use placement asset customization**: Placement asset customization allows you to tailor your ad copy to placements on Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp and Meta Audience Network. For example, you could use shorter ad copy on Stories placements, or more ‘brand-led’ copy on Instagram placements. [Learn more about placement asset customization](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1044825198987622).

- **Add text options:** Input multiple text options for the **Primary text**, **Headline** and **Description** fields when creating single image or video ads. This allows our ad system to optimize for delivery and performance using variations of the text options provided, based on individual preferences identified by our machine learning models. It’s a useful tool if you have several copy options and you’re unsure which creative resonates with different audiences.


## Best practices

Testing your ad is the best way to find what works for your audience, but these techniques can be effective.

- **Keep ad copy short:** Primary text should span 1-3 lines at most.

- **Communicate what you want people to do:** Communicating what you want people to do at a glance is the most important goal of your ad. All your text should be developed with this goal in mind. A range of call-to-action buttons are available, depending on your business goals.


## Considerations for text in ads

- Text in your ad may be truncated if it exceeds the character limitation. The recommended text length for most placements is 125 characters for the **Primary text** field, 40 characters for the **Headline** field and 25 characters for the **Description** field. However, your text may be further truncated across various placements and devices. We recommend keeping your text as short as possible to limit truncation.

- If you leave the text in your ad creative blank, text may be pulled from the website URL that you added as your ad destination and you may not be able to edit it. If you don’t want to use the text from your website URL, add your own text to your ad. Remember, if you use an existing post from your Facebook Page to create your ad, you can’t edit the text in your ad creative.

- If you use [Advantage+ creative](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/297506218282224) enhancements, such as text improvements, the text you upload may be adjusted. Some enhancements are turned on by default, and if you’ve opted in to test new optimizations in advertising settings, then test enhancements may be applied to eligible campaigns regardless of if you’re opted into Advantage+ creative at the ad level. You can turn off Advantage+ creative enhancements or opt out of new optimization testing at any time. Learn [how to turn off Advantage+ creative enhancements](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1082295769403815).


![](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/mci_ab/public/cms/?ab_b=e&ab_page=CMS&ab_entry=438223955063449&version=1666716831&transcode_extension=webp)

In line with our approach for testing new products, certain industry verticals such as Financial Services and Pharma/Health and ads for Housing, Employment or Financial Services/Credit(HEC), Social Issues, Elections, or Politics (SEIP), along with certain countries, may not have immediate access to all generative AI features. We know that advertisers are excited to start testing our generative AI features. While we are encouraged by the appetite to test and learn, we are taking the same cautious approach as we have with other similar product launches. Given the highly regulated environment that advertisers in these verticals operate in and the sensitivities around generative AI, our goal is to thoughtfully roll these features out based on feedback from both external policy stakeholders and advertisers. While we realize that there may be a differing level of risk tolerance among advertisers, we believe this approach will allow us to better understand potential risks and build the right safeguards for the use of generative AI in ads in Special Ad Categories and regulated industries. As we have updates, we will share more information at that time.

# Ideal length of social media posts: a guide for Facebook

[![Christine Tudhope](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/ddfc5c392c126db46c5b4e823d9dfbe6730c42591358ea8532ff48e85d3be53f?s=96&d=mm&r=g)](https://communications.wp.st-andrews.ac.uk/author/ct91/)

[Christine Tudhope](https://communications.wp.st-andrews.ac.uk/author/ct91/ "Posts by Christine Tudhope")

Thursday 25 January 2024

![Facebook logo](https://communications.wp.st-andrews.ac.uk/files/2023/04/Facebook-300x169.jpg)

What’s the one thing everyone who posts on social media needs **–** apart from a crack team of content creators? That’s right, it’s here at last, your saviour and guide to the ideal length of posts for every social network. ( _Please, hold your applause._)

In this blog we will focus on **Facebook** because, let’s face it, nobody has time to read, so we have broken our social media posts guide down to bitesized chunks on each network you are most likely to use on a daily basis.

This isn’t just a list of how long Facebook posts _can_ be: it’s evidence-based advice on the best Facebook post lengths to drive the most engagement.

If you want more likes, shares, video views, and comments ( _and what kind of monster doesn’t?!_), it’s pivotal to nail the length of your message.

Are you writing too much in your social media posts? Too little? Are your videos too long or not long enough? Read on for our curated research on the ideal character counts for Facebook posts (not to be confused with character limits) and other types of content.

### The ideal Facebook post length

While you have enough space to craft a novella on FB, the truth is shorter posts usually receive more likes, comments, and shares.

People like it when a message makes its point quickly and concisely. It’s satisfying.

### Organic posts length: 1 to 80 characters

We scoured the world wide web for research and the most recent study is from way back in 2016… an eternity in social media years, but it’s the best starting point we have.

In 2016, BuzzSumo analysed more than 800 million Facebook posts. Based on [their findings](http://buzzsumo.com/blog/ultimate-guide-facebook-engagement-2017/), posts with less than 50 characters “were more engaging than long posts”. According to another, more precise [study by Jeff Bullas](http://www.jeffbullas.com/10-powerful-tips-to-increase-fan-engagement-on-facebook/), posts with 80 characters or less receive 66 percent higher engagement.

There are a couple of reasons for this…

**Barrier to entry:** Facebook cuts off longer posts with an ellipsis, forcing users to click ‘See More’ to expand the text and read the entire message.

This extra step doesn’t seem like much, but it will drive down engagement. Every time you ask your audience to take action, a percentage of people will lose interest.

**Barrier to comprehension:** the longer a person reads, the harder his or her brain must work to process information. Content that demands less work to consume and understand will enjoy higher engagement rates.

### Paid posts length: 5 to 19 words

Every Facebook ad needs three types of content: a **Headline**, **Ad Text**, and a **Link Description**.

After analysing [752,626 Facebook adsback in 2018,](https://adespresso.com/blog/we-analyzed-37259-facebook-ads-and-heres-what-we-learned/) AdEspresso found that ads did best when the copy in each element was clear and concise.

According to the data, the ideal lengths for each element are:

- Headline, the first text people read — 5 words
- Ad Text, which appears above the ad — 19 words
- Link Description, which appears below the headline — 13 words

### Video length: 30 to 60 seconds

Sure, you _can_ upload a 240-minute video to Facebook… but will anyone actually watch it all the way through? With video, one of the primary measures of success is how long people watch, also known as your [video retention rate](https://www.facebook.com/facebookmedia/blog/understanding-how-your-videos-perform-on-facebook).

For viral content, [Facebook recommends](https://www.facebook.com/business/learn/lessons/video-best-practices-checklist) videos that are less than one minute or stories that are less than 20 seconds in length.

That being said, if you’re hoping to qualify for in-stream ads, you might want to linger a little longer — videos need to be more than three minutes to qualify.

Facebook also recommends videos over three minutes for episodic series, live streaming or story development.

Careful! Don’t go over the limit:

If Facebook posts feel harder to get right than they used to, you’re not imagining it. What worked even a year ago can now quietly sink your reach, and post length is one of the biggest reasons why.

Facebook’s algorithm has shifted toward rewarding clarity, engagement, and intent over filler. Long-winded posts get skimmed. Ultra-short posts can get ignored. The sweet spot sits somewhere in between, and it’s backed by data, not guesswork.

In this guide, we’ll break down the optimal Facebook post length that performs well today, how the algorithm treats short vs. long captions, and what businesses should focus on if they want more clicks, comments, and visibility without overthinking every post.

## Facebook Post Length in 2026: What’s Changed (and What Still Works)

By 2026, Facebook’s algorithm has become even more intent-driven. Instead of rewarding posts purely based on length, it now prioritizes **early engagement, meaningful interactions, and content clarity**, especially from business pages.

- **Short posts still win for visibility.** Posts under 80 characters continue to earn higher reach, particularly for updates, promotions, and service announcements. These posts are quick to read, easy to react to, and ideal for mobile users — who now make up the vast majority of Facebook traffic.
- **Medium-length posts perform best for trust and clicks.** Posts between 80 – 150 characters are outperforming longer captions when the goal is link clicks or comments. This range gives enough context to spark interest without triggering “scroll fatigue.”
- **Long posts need a purpose.** In 2026, posts over 200 characters only perform well when they’re clearly structured and value-driven — think educational content, storytelling, or expert advice. Walls of text still get deprioritized unless users actively engage.
- **Formatting matters more than ever.** Line breaks, emojis used sparingly, and a clear first sentence can significantly improve performance — often more than adding extra words.
- **AI-assisted feeds reward clarity.** With Facebook leaning further into AI-powered ranking, posts that communicate their point quickly and clearly are more likely to be surfaced to the right audience.

## What is the Optimal Facebook Post Length in 2026?

The best post length for Facebook in 2026 is between **40-80 characters**. Posts within this range have been shown to achieve the highest engagement rates, with a 66% increase in user interaction compared to longer posts. This brevity ensures that your content captures attention quickly, which is critical in the fast-scrolling environment of social media. Short, concise posts are more likely to be fully read and engaged with, leading to better performance on the platform.

![Best Facebook Post Length Sizes 2024](https://hookagency.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/best-facebook-post-length-sizes-2024.jpeg)

Stat via [Sprout Social’s Social Media Character Counter](https://sproutsocial.com/insights/social-media-character-counter/)

## What is the Best Time to Post on Facebook for 2026?

The best time to post on Facebook in 2026 is **early morning between 7-9 AM** and **late evening between 7-9 PM**. These time slots align with peak user activity, maximizing your post’s visibility and engagement. Data from Sprout Social indicates that posts made during these periods tend to receive higher interaction rates, making them ideal for reaching your audience when they are most active online.

**To-Do’s for Effective Facebook Posting in 2026**

1. **Prioritize Quality Over Quantity**: Short, impactful posts are key. Aim for 40-80 characters to boost engagement.
2. **Leverage Visuals**: Posts with images or videos get 2.3 times more engagement.
3. **Use Facebook Reels**: Short-form video content is king in 2026.
4. **Optimize Posting Times**: Post when your audience is most active—often early mornings or late evenings.
5. **Engage with Your Audience**: Respond to comments and messages promptly to build relationships.

## Why Facebook Post Length Matters

The length of your Facebook post can dramatically affect how well it performs. **According to Sprout Social, posts with 40-80 characters see the highest engagement rates,** with a sharp decline as the length increases. This doesn’t mean you can’t go longer—but if you do, make sure every word counts.

### Gary Vee’s Take on Content Length

Gary Vaynerchuk, a social media guru, emphasizes brevity. He notes, “People are scrolling faster than ever. If you can’t capture attention in the first three seconds, you’ve already lost.” This insight is crucial, especially in the crowded 2024 social media space.

### Latest Data on Post Length

HubSpot’s recent data backs this up, showing that posts under 80 characters have a 66% higher engagement rate than longer posts. The takeaway? Keep it short, sweet, and to the point.

### The Power of Visual Content

Visual content isn’t just a nice-to-have; it’s a must-have. Posts with images or videos consistently outperform text-only posts. According to a 2024 report from HubSpot, Facebook posts with images see 2.3 times more engagement than those without.

![Best Facebook image Sizes 2024](https://hookagency.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/best-facebook-image-sizes-2024.jpg)

### Alex Hormozi on Visuals

Alex Hormozi, a business strategist known for his no-nonsense approach, says, “Visuals do the selling for you. If you’re not using them, you’re leaving money on the table.” For home service businesses, this could mean sharing before-and-after photos, short video testimonials, or even time-lapse videos of your work.

### The Rise of Facebook Reels

Reels are the new frontier for Facebook content. According to Meta’s internal data, Reels are the fastest-growing content format, driving significant user engagement. In 2024, if you’re not leveraging Reels, you’re missing out on a huge opportunity to connect with your audience.

## Stats to Consider

- **Video posts**: 59% higher engagement than other post types (HubSpot, 2024).
- **Live video**: Users watch live videos 3 times longer than pre-recorded ones (Sprout Social, 2024).
- **Reels**: 22% more engagement than traditional video posts (Meta, 2024).

### Timing is Everything

When you post is almost as important as what you post. Data from Sprout Social suggests that the best times to post on Facebook in 2024 are early morning (around 7-9 AM) and late evening (around 7-9 PM). This timing aligns with when users are most active and likely to engage.

### Real-World Example

Consider a [roofing](https://hookagency.com/roofing-marketing/) company that posts at 7:30 AM, just as potential customers are starting their day. The post might include a short video of a recent project with a caption like, “Starting the day strong with a new roof installation! #RoofingExperts.” This kind of post is likely to catch the attention of homeowners who are in the market for similar services.

### Engage Like a Pro

Facebook’s algorithm in 2024 rewards active engagement. This means that simply posting isn’t enough—you need to interact with your audience. Responding to comments, engaging in group discussions, and even using Facebook Messenger to follow up with potential leads can all help boost your post’s visibility.

As Sprout Social’s 2024 report highlights, “Posts that generate conversations are prioritized in the newsfeed. Brands that actively engage with their audience will see higher reach and engagement.”

### Hormozi’s Engagement Tip

Alex Hormozi adds, “You have to be where your customers are. If they’re commenting on your posts, it’s an open invitation to start a conversation. Don’t just post and ghost—get in there and engage.”

## The Don’ts: What to Avoid in 2024

While it’s important to know what to do, it’s equally important to know what not to do. Here are some common mistakes that can hurt your Facebook performance in 2024:

1. **Avoid Overly Long Text**: Posts over 280 characters see a drop in engagement.
2. **Don’t Ignore Your Analytics**: Failing to review performance data can lead to repeated mistakes.
3. **Stop Posting Low-Quality Images**: Grainy or poorly composed images reflect poorly on your brand.
4. **Avoid Automated Responses**: Generic replies can make your brand seem impersonal and disengaged.

**Do long Facebook posts still work?**

Yes, but only when they’re intentional. Longer posts perform best when they educate, tell a story, or provide clear value. Unformatted blocks of text are still heavily deprioritized.

**Does Facebook penalize certain post lengths?**

Facebook doesn’t penalize length directly, but posts that fail to earn early engagement are shown to fewer people—longer posts are simply harder to engage with quickly.

**Are Facebook post length best practices different for businesses?**

Yes. Business pages tend to perform better with concise, clear messaging, especially for promotions, service updates, and offers. Personal storytelling can support longer captions, but clarity still wins.

Ultimately, the length of the text in your posts on social media properties is going to vary wildly from business to business. Where some businesses, like coaching services, tend to use a great chunk of a Facebook post’s built-in character limit, a high-end luxury item, may have just a few words that really capture their brand position.

## It’s less than you’d think.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*Df3bnkbtVsxPLmO5)

On Facebook, statuses of about 40–80 characters are the sweet spot. After that, the engagement, on average, starts to drop off. That’s not a lot. Especially considering that you can cram in as much as 63,206 characters that don’t include images and videos. But it does include emojis as characters, so you may want to bear that in mind.

However, the ideal length of text at the top of a Facebook Ad is just five words. Yes 5 words. This is based on a number of studies that showed that an ad starts to lose effective when the word count creeps above this. This means that your five words really need to count! It’s like you have to take a TikTok or Vine-like approach to your text. If you had just six seconds to get your message across, like in the old Vine app, or it’s replacement, Byte, you have to get very creative. So too, you need to be quite the wordsmith to get your impact across with just five words. There are people who are paid a lot in the world to do exactly that. It’s a fine art to write effective, and concise copy for social media.

Instagram allows you to have up to 2200 characters in the caption, which is heck of a lot to work with, but really, what is so important for you to say in a pictorial platform that you need 2200 characters to say it in? Social Report found that less than 125 characters do best in Instagram posts. But that doesn’t mean it will do best for you. Your hashtags can run well over your 125 character guideline and help tell the story in your first comment, or lower on your captions.

## Tease, rather than explain

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*lrJP6rR3I-UXVldl)

I keep saying this, because it is important, your business may vary from this, but there are some guidelines you should take on board and try with your posts. One over-arching theme I like to repeat with our clients, is that no one is coming to social media to read what you have to say about your business unless they already have a strong relationship with you, or you are in such a specialty niche that produces a very special thing that is in high demand, but supplied in small amounts.

The implication here is that if you are talking to potentially new customers in a Facebook or Instagram ad, or a post on LinkedIn, the post isn’t the place to get deep into product descriptions or thoughts and feelings. I was so glad when LinkedIn cut down the character limit on their posts. There was this habit for coaches and motivational gurus to flood the feed with long, meandering stories that would carry on and on and on.

Think of business posts on social media as a kind of “teaser.” You don’t need to tell the whole story, you just need to introduce it with a compelling enough introduction to make someone want to find more somewhere else. That “somewhere else” could be an article on a website, a longer format video on YouTube, or a link to an article on LinkedIn, a note on Facebook, or downloadable report, whitepaper or e-book.

## The language of your audience

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*vSMy1ZynO3wTEtKx)

Did you notice how I used the word, “meandering” a little earlier. There is a good chance that a number of you didn’t understand what I meant by it, or you had as vague idea of what it meant in the context of what I was saying. While I deliberately inserted that word in there to mention it again here, it’s a word that I should not have used in a setting like this. The type of reader or listener that I am trying to communicate to here, is not likely to understand that kind of word. In fact, they may find my use of that a little pretentious. Which is also another pretentious word. How many people even know what it means when they use it in conversation?

The point here is to know who you are talking to, so you can use the same language and tone that they use, or at least feel comfortable with reading or listening to being used. If your audience was academic, then you would use terms, phrasing and words that would suit that audience, right? But you wouldn’t try to use those words at the local footy club awards night, would you? There is a time for Shakespeare, and there’s a time for Johnno the full forward who likes to sink a few after a game on a Saturday afternoon during the season.

There are also gender considerations to make. If you are speaking to a very politically sensitive group of people or writing for those who have a strong leaning towards a particular point of view when it comes to language, you may need to adjust your language and tone; not just the length of your posts. You don’t want to trigger a flashback in a post that you wanted to use to trigger someone to buy something from you.

## So what’s next?

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/0*oynYvgLEMrlcHlS7)

While there are a number of considerations to make when it comes to the lengths of your social media posts, these will tend to be tied more closely to the language and tone of your target audience. Character-length and word-count may be important for an essay, but it’s more important on social posts to ensure that your message is abundantly clear and does something to inspire some kind of response. And where you can, try and do that in as few actual words as you possibly can!

# The Ideal Length of a Social Media Post for Medical Practices

![Social media posts](https://virginiacreativegroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/VCG-Blog-Social-Media-Post-Length_400x400.png)In the world of social media, content is king—but the length of that content can make all the difference, especially for medical practices. Whether you’re sharing health tips, promoting services, or engaging with patients, finding the perfect balance between brevity and informativeness is key. So, how long should your social media posts be to maximize engagement and effectively communicate your message? Let’s dive into the ideal post lengths for various social media platforms and how they can benefit your medical practice.

#### **1\. Facebook: Keeping It Short and Sweet**

**Ideal Length**: 40-80 characters

Facebook is a versatile platform that allows for longer posts, but shorter ones tend to perform better. Posts with **40-80 characters** generate the highest engagement rates. This length is enough to convey a clear message without overwhelming your audience. For medical practices, this could be a quick health tip, a brief announcement, or a call to action.

**Example**: “Flu season is here! Schedule your vaccine today for a healthier tomorrow.”

**Why It Works**: [Short posts](https://www.agorapulse.com/social-media-lab/does-the-length-of-facebook-posts-matter/) are easily digestible and can capture attention quickly, making them perfect for patients who are scrolling through their feed.

#### **2\. Twitter: Brevity Is Best**

**Ideal Length**: 71-100 characters

Twitter’s character limit encourages brevity, but the sweet spot for engagement is between **71-100 characters**. This length allows you to be concise while still providing enough information to spark interest. For medical practices, use this space to share quick updates, health facts, or links to more detailed content.

**Example**: “Did you know? Regular exercise can lower your risk of heart disease by up to 50%! #HeartHealth”

**Why It Works**: Short Tweets are more likely to be retweeted, favorited, and engaged with, helping your message reach a broader audience.

#### **3\. Instagram: Captions with Impact**

**Ideal Length**: 138-150 characters

On Instagram, visuals are the star, but a well-crafted caption can enhance the message. While Instagram allows for longer captions, **138-150 characters** is the ideal length for maximizing engagement. This gives you enough room to provide context to your image or video without losing the attention of your audience.

**Example**: “Stay hydrated! Drinking water is essential for your health. How much water have you had today? 💧 #HealthyLiving”

**Why It Works**: A concise caption paired with a compelling image or video can make your post more engaging and memorable, encouraging users to like, comment, and share.

#### **4\. LinkedIn: Professional Yet Punchy**

**Ideal Length**: 50-100 characters

LinkedIn is a professional network, so posts should be clear and to the point. The optimal length for a LinkedIn post is **50-100 characters**. This allows you to convey your message professionally while keeping it brief enough to hold the attention of busy professionals.

**Example**: “Join our webinar on the latest in orthopedic surgery. Register now! #MedicalProfessionals”

**Why It Works**: Short, concise posts resonate well on LinkedIn, where professionals are looking for valuable information quickly.

#### **5\. YouTube: Descriptive Titles and Snappy Descriptions**

**Ideal Title Length**: 70 characters **Ideal Description Length**: 100-150 characters (first part visible)

For YouTube, the title should be around **70 characters** to ensure it’s fully visible in search results and on mobile devices. Descriptions should be concise but informative, with the most important information placed within the first **100-150 characters**.

**Example Title**: “Understanding Knee Pain: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment Options”

**Example Description**: “Learn about the common causes of knee pain and how to manage it effectively. Watch our full video for expert tips. #KneePain #Orthopedics”

**Why It Works**: An engaging title and a concise, informative description can boost your video’s visibility and click-through rate, driving more traffic to your content.

### **Why Length Matters for Medical Practices**

For medical practices, the ideal length of a social media post isn’t just about following trends—it’s about effectively communicating important information in a way that resonates with your audience. Patients and followers are more likely to engage with content that is clear, concise, and relevant to their needs.

- **Patient Engagement**: Shorter posts are easier to read and more likely to be shared, increasing your practice’s reach.
- **Clarity**: Clear, concise messaging helps ensure that your audience understands the information, which is particularly important in healthcare communication.
- **Trust**: Consistently delivering well-crafted, informative content can build trust with your audience, making them more likely to turn to your practice for their healthcare needs.

The ideal length of a social media post for medical practices varies by platform, but the overarching principle remains the same: keep it concise and impactful. By tailoring your content to the specific characteristics of each platform, you can enhance patient engagement, convey your message effectively, and strengthen your online presence.

# Social Media Cheat Sheet: Character Limits & Posting Parameters

[Home](https://www.aaepa.com/) » [Law Firm Marketing](https://www.aaepa.com/category/law_firm_marketing/) » **Social Media Cheat Sheet: Character Limits & Posting Parameters**

![](https://www.aaepa.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/Character-150x150.jpg)Creating a social media marketing calendar for your law firm can certainly be challenging! There’s so much to consider when deciding how best to adapt your content for each social media channel: engaging topics, appropriate content formats, posting schedules, the best times to post on each platform.

If all that wasn’t enough, each social media network has its own set of specifications and maximum character lengths, which seem to change on a weekly basis. That’s why we put together the latest, most up-to-date social media post specs in this handy guide. Read on to learn more about the specifications for each platform, along with some advice about best practices.

**Google My Business**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Posts | 1,500 max, no minimum |
| Title | 58 characters max |

Posts can be up to 1,500 characters, but only the first 100 words are visible. The rest can be seen once the post is clicked on, but because of GMB’s design, that’s not very intuitive. [According to Google](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7390603?hl=en&ref_topic=7343035), the ideal length of a GMB post is between 150 – 300 characters.

**Facebook**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Username | 50 characters max |
| Page Description | 155 characters max |
| Posts | 63,206 characters max |
| Comments | 8,000 characters max |
| Video size | Up to 10 GB |
| Duration | 240 mins max |
| Format | MP4 recommended, but any format can be used |
| Image Upload Size | 30 MB max |

Of course, just because Facebook allows 63K+ characters doesn’t mean it’s a good idea. The chances of visitors reading the entire post of that length are slim. Social media experts, including marketing giant [Hubspot](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/character-count-guide), consider 40 – 50 characters to be the ideal length for a post.

**Twitter**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Tweets | 280 characters max |
| Direct Messages | 10,000 characters max |
| Image Upload Size | 5 MB max |
| Resolution | 1500 x 500 pixels |

Although Twitter has increased the character limits from 140 to 280 characters, shorter tweets get more engagement. Studies show that tweets that are 71 – 100 characters in length are liked and retweeted more than longer posts. Remember, @ mentions, gifs, and images don’t take away from a tweet’s character limits, but links do, though they’ll be shortened to 23 characters.

**LinkedIn**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Status | 700 characters max |
| Articles | 120,000 characters max |
| Group Discussions | 2,000 characters max |

The ideal length for a LinkedIn status is around 100 characters. The “See More” button cuts off messages at about 140 characters. For articles, the recommendation is 3,000 characters.

**Instagram**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Caption | 2,20 characters max |
| Bio | 150 characters max |
| Username | 30 characters max |
| Hashtags | 30 hashtags max |
| Image Size | 30 MB max |
| Image Aspect Ration | 1:91:1 to 16:9 |
| Video Upload | 4 GB max |
| Video Duration | 60 seconds max |

Again, the character limit is probably more than you want to use. Using the full 2,200 characters means your visitor will need to click on the “See more” button to view your entire post, so it’s better to shorten your captions. Under 125 characters is recommended so that your entire caption is visible in the Instagram feed.

**YouTube**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Video Title | 100 characters max |
| Description | 5,000 characters max |
| Video length | Up to 12 hours |

Note, your video title will likely cut off at 70 characters in most search results, so it’s best to keep your titles short and include your most important keywords at the beginning of the title.

The video description is the one place you should make full use of the allotted characters. YouTube is the third most popular search engine, following Google Search and Google Images, so including important keywords in your video description is a good way to improve your rankings in search results.

Capturing social media audience’s attention is a constant challenge for law firms, made more difficult by the constantly changing rules and regulations. Bookmark this cheat sheet to quickly refer back to the info you need for a successful social media marketing plan and don’t forget to also review our [Online Marketing Images Cheat Sheet](https://www.aaepa.com/2021/01/online-marketing-images-cheat-sheet/).
